cues.en: Something else. So they were very skillful. Yeah. But
cues.zh: 还有一件事，他们确实很有本事。不过，

cues.en: they did show us. Yeah. So,
cues.zh: 他们确实给我们看了。对，所以，

cues.en: and it's good that they showed us because the technology crashed and burned at Xerox.
cues.zh: 幸好他们给我们看了，因为这项技术在施乐公司彻底失败了。

cues.en: They used to call the- What's that? No, I was just- Why? Yeah, why. Oh, very, I actually thought a lot about that, and I learned more about that with John Scully later on, and I think I understand it now pretty well. What happens is,
cues.zh: 他们以前把它叫做——怎么了？不，我只是——为什么？对，为什么。我其实认真想过这个问题，后来和约翰·斯卡利共事时，又对它有了更多了解。我觉得现在我已经相当明白了。事情是这样的：

cues.en: like with John Scully,
cues.zh: 就像约翰·斯卡利那样，

cues.en: John came from PepsiCo,
cues.zh: 约翰来自百事公司，

cues.en: and they at most would change their product, you know, once every ten years. I mean to them a new product was like a new size bottle, right? So if you were a product person,
cues.zh: 他们顶多十年才会改一次产品。对他们来说，新产品大概就是换个尺寸的瓶子，对吧？所以，如果你是负责产品的人，

cues.en: you couldn't change the course of that company very much. So who influenced the success of PepsiCo? The sales and marketing people. Therefore they were the ones that got promoted and therefore they were the ones that ran the company.
cues.zh: 你根本没法大幅改变公司的发展方向。那么，谁影响了百事公司的成功？销售和市场营销人员。因此，他们得到晋升，最后也由他们掌管公司。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 好吧，

cues.en: for PepsiCo that might have been okay,
cues.zh: 这对百事可乐来说或许无所谓，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: it turns out the same thing can happen in technology companies that get monopolies,
cues.zh: 事实证明，同样的情况也会发生在形成垄断的科技公司身上，

cues.en: like, oh, IBM and Xerox.
cues.zh: 比如 IBM 和 Xerox。

cues.en: If you were a product person at IBM or Xerox,
cues.zh: 如果你是 IBM 或 Xerox 的产品人员，

cues.en: so you make a better copy or a better computer. So what? When you have a monopoly market share,
cues.zh: 就算你做出了更好的复印机或更好的电脑，那又怎样？当你拥有垄断性的市场份额时，

cues.en: the company's not any more successful.
cues.zh: 公司并不会因此变得更成功。

cues.en: So the people that can make the company more successful are sales and marketing people.
cues.zh: 所以，能让公司更成功的人反而是销售和市场人员。

cues.en: And they end up running the companies. And the product people get driven out of the decision making forums.
cues.zh: 最终由他们接管了公司，而产品人则被逐出了决策圈。

cues.en: And the companies forget
cues.zh: 于是这些公司遗忘了

cues.en: what it means to make great products.
cues.zh: 做出优秀产品究竟意味着什么。

cues.en: It sort of the product
cues.zh: 这种产品的

cues.en: sensibility
cues.zh: 敏锐度，

cues.en: and the product genius that brought them to that monopolistic position gets rotted out
cues.zh: 以及曾将他们推向垄断地位的产品天赋，逐渐被侵蚀殆尽，

cues.en: by people running these companies who have no conception
cues.zh: 取而代之的是掌管这些公司的人，他们对产品的优劣

cues.en: of a good product versus a bad product. They have no conception of the craftsmanship
cues.zh: 毫无概念。他们完全不懂将一个好点子打磨成好产品

cues.en: that's required to take a good idea and turn it into a good product. And they really have no feeling in their hearts usually about wanting to really help the customers.
cues.zh: 需要怎样的工匠精神。而且在他们内心深处，通常也根本没有真正想要帮助用户的热情。

cues.en: So that's what happened at Xerox. The people at Xerox PARK used to call the people that ran Xerox toner heads.
cues.zh: 施乐公司当年就是这样。施乐帕克研究中心的人，过去常把施乐的管理层叫做“墨粉脑袋”。

cues.en: And they just had, and these toner heads would come out to Xerox PARK and they just had no clue about what they were seeing. And for our audience, toner is what? Oh, toner. Toner is what you put into a copier.
cues.zh: 而这些墨粉脑袋会跑到施乐帕克来，却完全看不懂自己眼前的东西。对咱们听众来说，墨粉是什么？哦，墨粉。墨粉就是你放进复印机里的东西。

cues.en: Yeah, you know the toner that you add to an industrial copier? The black stuff. The black stuff, yeah. So
cues.zh: 对，就是往工业复印机里加的那种墨粉？黑色的东西。黑色的东西，没错。所以

cues.en: basically they were copier heads. They just had no clue about
cues.zh: 说白了，他们就是一群复印机脑袋。他们对计算机、对计算机能干什么，

cues.en: a computer or what it could do. And so they just grabbed
cues.zh: 完全一窍不通。于是他们就这么

cues.en: defeat from the greatest victory in the computer industry.
cues.zh: 把计算机行业史上最伟大的一场胜利，拱手变成了失败。

cues.en: Xerox could have owned the entire computer industry today.
cues.zh: 施乐本可以在今天拥有整个计算机行业。

cues.en: Could have been, you know, a company 10 times its size. Could have been IBM.
cues.zh: 本来可以成为一家规模大十倍的公司，你知道的。本来可以成为 IBM。

cues.en: Could have been the IBM of the nineties. Could have been the Microsoft of the nineties.
cues.zh: 本来可以成为九十年代的 IBM，也可以成为九十年代的微软。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: but anyway, that's all ancient history. It doesn't really matter anymore. Sure.
cues.zh: 不过，这些都已经是陈年往事了。现在已经不重要了。是啊。
